statements.statement: At 1538, a Field Op detected a sweet gas smell near the suction scrubber skid at Compressor Station 4. Upon investigation, the 3-inch vent on the scrubber discharge was found to be open. The valve was tagged as 'closed' but was actually about 1/4 turn off seat. The compressor was running without a trip during this time. The valve was secured and the incident was reported. The site is now stable.
statements.report_words: Just rolled up to Station 4 around 1530 for the quarterly valve grease job. At 1538 I caught a sweet gas smell near the suction scrubber skid. Walked the lines, found the 3-inch vent on the scrubber discharge was open. Valve was tagged 'closed' but the handle was about 1/4 turn off seat. No flowmeter on the vent so no number on volume. Same vent was found open on this skid last October. Valve handle was wide open and the tag was missing. Compressor was running the whole time, no trip. Secured the valve and called it in. Site's stable now.

statements.statement: The night shift at Sundre station reported a fire on the east compressor pad around 21:00 on May 26. The crew saw flames, pulled the E-stop, and called 911. The local fire department arrived and extinguished the fire quickly. The fire appeared to have started in the inlet scrubber skid, with heat discoloration on the separator shell and some wiring harness melting off the scrubber control panel. No product was involved in the fire, and everything remained inside the pipe. A temporary line is being run through the unit to maintain downstream pressure, and the scrubber will need to be replaced as soon as possible.
statements.report_words: The night shift at Sundre station reported a fire on the east compressor pad around 21:00 on May 26. Crew saw flames, pulled the E-stop, called 911. Local FD showed up, knocked it down quick. Looked like the inlet scrubber skid caught. Heat discoloration on the separator shell and some wiring harness melted off the scrubber control panel. No product hit the fire, everything stayed inside pipe. Still running a temp line through the unit to keep downstream pressure up; will need to swap the scrubber ASAP.
